editorial:
You're dropped into a wealthy marriage that looks perfect from the outside but is quietly falling apart. Vic and Melinda Van Allen live in a gorgeous home, yet their relationship runs on a strange agreement: she can see other men, and he won't ask questions. The tension builds slowly as her lovers start turning up dead, and everyone around them begins to wonder if Vic is just a patient husband or something much darker. The mood is cold and uncomfortable, with every dinner party feeling like a trap.

Ben Affleck plays Vic with a flat, unsettling calm that keeps you guessing, while Ana de Armas brings a wild, unpredictable energy to Melinda. The pacing is slow and deliberate, which works for the mystery but may test your patience if you want fast thrills. The biggest strength is the creepy atmosphere and the way small moments feel loaded with threat. On the downside, the story can feel repetitive and the ending may leave you wanting more. If you enjoy slow-burn psychological thrillers, this is worth a night in.
endingExplained: In the final act, Vic kills Melinda's latest lover and hides the body. When a neighbor sees him, Vic tries to silence him too, but the man escapes and tells the police. Melinda realizes what Vic has done and seems oddly turned on by it. The movie ends with the couple driving away together, their toxic bond stronger than ever, leaving you unsure if she will be his next victim or his willing partner.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark marriage thrillers and slow-burn mysteries.
